events.summary: Created as the child design record for stable stacked-port identities and route selection before path rendering returns.
Activated for the routing-model discussion; no production or prototype routing implementation is authorized by this record alone.
Rejected the terse j:<u>:<v> and p-j:<u>:<v>:q:<q>,r:<r> identifier draft. Recorded a clearer, provisional path-segment grammar for user review.
Refined the provisional grammar so junction and slot axes remain named inside the identifier, improving direct inspection without changing canonical coordinate math.
Implemented the accepted identity grammar in the isolated prototype: generated slot, junction, and concrete slot-port IDs now back its DOM data attributes.
Studio npm run build passed after the identity implementation. No unit-test runner is configured in the Studio package; no path rendering was restored.

Generated-ID verification found 210 unique concrete port keys across the 35-slot prototype and a canonical junction with three distinct slot-owned ports. Studio lint passed with only three pre-existing fast-refresh warnings.
Implemented the first visible routing slice: sample edges render as direct, nearest vertex-port SVG segments with directional arrow markers.
Fresh local preview visibly confirmed both sample routes. Studio npm run build and npm run lint passed; lint retained only three pre-existing fast-refresh warnings.
Changed the direct-route visual grammar at the user's direction: routes are plain solid cyan lines with no arrow, dash, or glow decoration.
Fresh local preview confirmed solid routes remain distinct from slot frames. Studio npm run build and npm run lint passed; lint retained only three pre-existing fast-refresh warnings.
Moved r-004 to slot/q4-r2 in the isolated placement bridge. The direct-route baseline recalculates its nearest vertex-port pair from the slot coordinates.
Studio npm run build passed; isolated preview accessibility state and screenshot both located r-004 in slot/q4-r2.
Replaced direct endpoint segments with a complete prototype slot-port graph traversal: adjacent perimeter-port links plus zero-cost stacked-port transfers at shared junctions.

Studio npm run build and lint passed; the isolated preview showed routes stepping through frame vertices rather than cutting across open canvas. Lint retained only three existing fast-refresh warnings outside the prototype.

Recorded exclusive input/output traffic roles as a future directional-port slice. Availability remains independent: an open input accepts inbound traffic only, and an open output emits outbound traffic only.

Implemented dynamic directional ports: routes claim open ports as exclusive input or output states, and later routes cannot reverse a claimed role. Markers now expose availability and role data attributes with distinct input/output styling.

Studio build and lint passed. A fresh isolated preview showed cyan output and purple input markers while retaining r-004 at slot/q4-r2; lint retained only three existing fast-refresh warnings outside the prototype.

Implemented inner-turn port allocation. Each non-collinear previous/current/next junction triple now selects the current port owned by the unique slot inside the turn, separately from input/output traffic role.
Studio build passed and fresh preview showed amber inner-turn allocation rings alongside directed port markers. The documented u9-v4 to u10-v5 to u9-v6 example resolves to slot/q2-r1.
Clarified the allocation boundary: an inner-turn marker represents foreign pass-through geometry and therefore omits data-traffic-role while retaining availability and its amber allocation marker.
Studio npm run build and npm run lint passed after allocated markers stopped emitting data-traffic-role. Lint retained only three existing fast-refresh warnings outside the prototype.

Corrected the allocation traffic-role test: compare each allocated port's slotId to the allocating route's targetSlotId. Only foreign turn allocations omit data-traffic-role; destination-slot allocations retain it.
Studio npm run build and npm run lint passed after the destination-slot ownership correction. Lint retained only three existing fast-refresh warnings outside the prototype.

Replaced the incorrect destination-slot exception with the logical route-spine rule: source anchor, one inward 120-degree slot-owned anchor per middle junction, and target anchor. Only source output and target input emit traffic roles.
Added data-port-connection-count for each concrete SlotPortId. Counts come from logical route-spine anchors and never aggregate a shared junction's stacked ports.
Studio npm run build and npm run lint passed after per-port connection counts were added. Lint retained only three existing fast-refresh warnings outside the prototype.
Defined connection count as distinct route-spine use per concrete SlotPortId, so a looping route cannot inflate one port's count through repeated visits.
Studio npm run build and npm run lint passed after distinct per-port count handling. Lint retained only three existing fast-refresh warnings outside the prototype.
Removed the gold turn-allocation ring while preserving allocation data attributes, availability, and endpoint traffic-role presentation.
Studio npm run build and npm run lint passed after removing the gold turn-allocation ring. Lint retained only three existing fast-refresh warnings outside the prototype.

Preserved the supplying output port across each junction transfer in transient graph state, then added a collinearity cost that prefers a straight-ahead perimeter continuation over its sideward sibling.
Studio npm run build and npm run lint passed. Direct route evaluation confirmed r-002 begins port/junction/u7-v4/slot/q2-r0 then port/junction/u6-v3/slot/q1-r1, rather than the u6-v5 alternative.

Diagnosed current r-002 routing: all source outputs start at zero cost, local unsigned collinearity does not choose the closest source connection, and the rendered turn-allocation spine can differ from the raw traversal.
Extracted the existing graph route policy behind HoneycombRouteVariant. Its ordered concrete port hooks are now the canvas-rendering contract, with first origin/output and final destination/input.
Studio npm run build passed after route-variant extraction.
Added visual-only canvas-end slots around the workflow lattice. Their outward concrete ports are closed, and they are excluded from node placement and route traversal.
Studio npm run build passed after adding canvas-end slots.
Direct adjacent workflow edges now suppress their shared frame-side strokes and render one midpoint side-control hexagon with CSS-controlled geometry and styling.
Studio npm run build passed after adding adjacency seam detection and the visual side-control.
